title: Accelerate your AI journey with Azure AI model catalog: Sharmila Chokalingam
talk_summary: A product-marketing walkthrough of Azure AI model catalog and AI Studio: browsing 1,600+ models, serverless vs managed-compute deployment, a standardized inference API/SDK so you can swap models by changing only the endpoint, playground with add-your-data, prompt flow with a rephrasing step and model variants for evaluation, plus enterprise privacy/security claims and three customer stories. It is mostly a vendor demo; the transferable parts are the standardized model-swap interface, the query-rephrasing-before-RAG trick, and variant-based evaluation.

takeaways.technique: Standardized inference schema so models are swappable by endpoint only
takeaways.what_they_do: They force all catalog models behind one REST schema and one SDK, so switching providers means changing only the endpoint/key while the rest of the codebase is untouched.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all you have to have is a different endpoint and every endpoint has the same API structure and the same SDK structure

takeaways.technique: Prompt-flow variants + side-by-side evaluation across models
takeaways.what_they_do: They clone the same flow with different model connections (Command R vs Llama 3 vs Mistral Large, Ada vs Cohere embeddings) and run evaluations to compare outputs on the same inputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can create these variance and try to see the evaluation results

takeaways.what_they_do: Before the RAG lookup step they expand the user's terse prompt into a longer, more verbose query, which they say retrieves better context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we try to make it more verbos by rephrasing it because we've seen better result results of rag with that

takeaways.technique: Serverless per-token vs managed-compute per-hour deployment choice
takeaways.what_they_do: They split deployment into serverless (pay per input/output token, no capacity management) and managed compute (own GPUs, pay per VM-hour, you manage quota/capacity).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you basically pay for the VMS per hour and you're responsible for the quota management capacity management

takeaways.technique: Allow/deny-list policy separating dev/test/prod model access
takeaways.what_they_do: Azure policy integration lets them allow-list or deny-list model collections and apply different policies per environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have allow list or deny list patterns and you can split out which model collections you want access to

takeaways.technique: Continuous evaluation as an ongoing practice, not one-time
takeaways.what_they_do: In the EY story they stress that using AI is not one-time and requires continuous evaluation of performance plus responsible-AI checks before production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's not AI using AI in their use cases is not like a one-time thing they need to do continuous evaluation
takeaways.numbers: EY chat adopted by 275,000 employees (marketing figure, not a technique result)
